newsitem.title: USA: US close to capacity but not overheating-Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: US close to capacity but not overheating-Greenspan.

text.p: The U.S. economy is running very close to capacity but so far it is not overheating, Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said on Wednesday.
"The economy at this particular stage in time ... is clearly running very close to any measure of capacity," he told a House Banking subcommittee.
"It is not," he added, "one that is clearly overheated, one in which inflation is clearly accelerating."
The inflationary risks, however, remain on the upside, as they have been over the last year, especially since July, Greenspan said.

Fed policymakers have forecast that inflation will stay low and stable this year. But Greenspan said that forecasts per se were not what determined monetary policy, but rather where the risks to the economy lie.
"We do not raise rates for the purpose of slowing the economy," the Fed chief added. "When we raise rates, it usually is for the purpose of stabilizing elements which threaten growth."
Greenspan argued that while a little inflation may sound harmless, it is bad for the economy because it leads to faster and faster price rises that eventually undermine growth.
The Fed chief though expressed scepticism about the usefulness of the non-accelerating inflationary rate of unemployment (NAIRU) economic concept for monetary policy.
The NAIRU theory posits that there is an unemployment rate at which inflation neither accelerates nor decelerates.
